name: erc721_patterns
description: Reentrancy in NFT mint function via _safeMint callback bypassing supply/limit checks
question: The source file in `source` contains a Solidity ERC-721 contract whose payable mint function calls `_safeMint` (or `_mint`) to an externally supplied recipient before updating the state variable that enforces a max-supply cap or per-wallet mint limit (e.g. incrementing `_nextTokenId`, `mintedCount[msg.sender]`, or `totalSupply` only after the mint call), with no reentrancy guard applied, so a malicious contract's `onERC721Received` callback can reenter the mint function and mint tokens beyond the intended cap or repeatedly consume the same paid value.
criteria: mint function invokes _safeMint or _mint before incrementing a supply/limit counter
no nonReentrant modifier or reentrancy lock on the mint function
state variable enforcing maxSupply, perWallet limit, or nextTokenId is written after the external mint call
payable mint function checks msg.value/price but relies on later state update for limit enforcement
recipient address for _safeMint is attacker-controllable (msg.sender or external parameter)
